caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:000165
attempts.entry_title: Hippocampal LFP after suppressing DG and CA3 interneurons (Aery Jones et al. 2021)
attempts.summary: Few of the paper's main findings on suppressing PV+ and SST+ interneurons in mouse hippocampus held up in this data. The PV+ rise in CA1 sharp-wave ripple frequency reproduced, and the SST+ rise in fast gamma frequency held in CA3 and DG but not CA1. The opposing effects of the two on ripple rate, the PV+ rises in sharp-wave amplitude and slow gamma power, and the SST+ rise in fast gamma power did not reproduce. As deposited, one cohort has every CNO session after its vehicle sessions, and its empty-vector control mice also change with CNO. Histology, slice recordings and fast ripples are not in the dataset and could not be tested.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Aery Jones et al. (2021) on dandiset 000165, which holds the LFP, MUA spike times and position of PV-Cre, SST-Cre, PV-Cre/SST-Cre and empty vector mice in home cage and linear track sessions after vehicle or CNO. It tests the SWR, CA3 SWR and dentate spike features at rest, the gamma, theta and MUA features during running, the double suppression, empty vector and sex comparisons, and the CSD during SWRs of cohort 1, with the paper's linear mixed models.

outcomes.statement: hM4D expression is highly co-localized with PV and SST and extends throughout DG and CA3, with no expression in CA1 or CA2.
outcomes.source: Results, Recording in vivo hippocampal LFP, paragraph 1; Figure 1D, Figure S1A-C, Table S1
outcomes.quote: HM4D expression was highly co-localized with PV and SST expression (Figure S1A–C and Table S1) and extended throughout DG and CA3 from dorsal to ventral hippocampus, with no expression in CA1 or CA2
outcomes.notes: Histological cell counts are not in the dandiset (its files hold LFP, MUA spike times and position) and the paper names no other archive for them.

outcomes.statement: In ex vivo slices CNO hyperpolarizes hM4D-expressing PV+ and SST+ interneurons by 8.6 +/- 1.3 mV and changes their input resistance by 31.3 +/- 9.9 MOhm.
outcomes.source: Results, Recording in vivo hippocampal LFP, paragraph 1; Figure S1E-F
outcomes.quote: hyperpolarized resting membrane potentials by 8.6 ± 1.3mV (Figure S1E), and decreased input resistance by 31.3 ± 9.9 MΩ (Figure S1F)
outcomes.notes: The slice patch-clamp recordings are not in the dandiset and the paper names no other archive for them.

outcomes.statement: During SWRs, current source density sources and sinks in CA1 stratum radiatum increase when either PV+ or SST+ interneurons are suppressed, with no difference between genotypes.
outcomes.source: Figure 2E-F; Results, SWR signatures, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: During SWRs, CSD sources and sinks in stratum radiatum – the layer of CA3 input – increased when either PV+ or SST+ interneurons were suppressed (Figure 2C–F)
outcomes.notes: Cohort 1, 5 PV-Cre and 4 SST-Cre mice, 62 sessions. With PV+ suppression the peak CA1-sr source (+6540 file units per mm2, p = 4.4e-11) and sink (+16200, p = 0.0014) increase; with SST+ suppression both rise in every mouse but not significantly (source p = 0.0078, sink p = 0.015). The genotype tests are not significant (p = 0.65 and 0.23), as claimed. Two of four treatment effects hold; the partial rule needs three. With the code's 5 SD SWRs and the log transform (reading b) the SST-Cre source is significant (p = 0.0012), three of four.
deviations: CSD as minus the second difference across depth of the (a + 2b + c)/4 smoothed LFP, spacing 50 um from the probe name (A1x32-6mm-50), in file units per mm2; peak source and sink over the CA1-sr sites in the 100 ms after SWR onset (criterion; Methods, Analysis of neural data, paragraph 4).
SWRs as in the rest notebook (3 SD, boundaries where the envelope crosses its mean, edge and artifact rules).
Holm decided with the rest notebook's SST-Cre p-values (the family stops at its second rank, 0.05/23); the two CSD comparisons are not recomputed with the others.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing either interneuron class increases the recruitment of DG and CA3 MUA to CA1 SWRs, but not of CA1 MUA.
outcomes.source: Figure 3B; Results, SWR signatures, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: suppressing either class increased the extent to which DG and CA3, but not CA1, MUA increased during SWRs (Figure 3B)
outcomes.notes: With spike times shifted per session to the SWRs, CA1 MUA recruitment does not change (PV-Cre p = 0.12, SST-Cre p = 0.30), as claimed, but CA3 (p = 0.80 and 0.59) and DG (p = 0.094 and 0.094, PV-Cre coefficient negative) do not increase. With the deposited spike times no CA3 or DG increase is significant either. 14 PV-Cre and 14 SST-Cre mice.
deviations: The deposited spike times are offset from the LFP by a session-specific lag (see findings). The main reading shifts each session's spike times by the lag of the CA1 MUA peak around SWR midpoints (sessions whose peak is under 3 times the median are left out, 50 of 311); this is an assumption.
MUA at the site labelled "mua" in each region (Methods, Analysis of neural data, paragraph 5, the site with the highest MUA).

outcomes.statement: Suppressing PV+ interneurons increases CA1 SWR rate while suppressing SST+ interneurons decreases it, and the two effects differ significantly.
outcomes.source: Figure 3C; Results, SWR signatures, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Suppressing PV+ interneurons increased SWR rate while suppressing SST+ interneurons decreased SWR rate, and these effects were significantly different between genotypes (Figure 3C)
outcomes.notes: Reading (b) of the log transform gives a significant PV-Cre increase (0.33 log units, p = 1.0e-08); reading (a), untransformed, gives +4.2 SWRs/min with p = 0.014, not significant after Holm. The SST-Cre effect is not a decrease (p = 0.37 and 0.84) and the genotype test is not significant (p = 0.67 and 0.093). The 5 SD variant agrees. Empty vector mice also have a higher rate on CNO days (23.8 against 28.9 per min; LMM p = 0.0017), which points to session order (see findings).
deviations: SWR boundaries where the smoothed envelope crosses its mean (Frank lab convention, Cheng and Frank 2008, which the Methods cite); the Methods give only the 3 SD, 15 ms threshold.
14 PV-Cre and 14 SST-Cre mice, not 16 each; four mice have only CNO-labelled sessions.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing either interneuron class decreases the proportion of SWRs that occur in chains (within 200 ms of another SWR).
outcomes.source: Figure 3D; Results, SWR signatures, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: There was also a decrease in the proportion of SWRs that participated in chains (Figure 3D) in both genotypes
outcomes.notes: PV-Cre p = 0.48; SST-Cre decrease with p = 0.0064, not significant after Holm. With the code's 5 SD events the SST-Cre decrease is significant (p = 0.00044) and PV-Cre is not (p = 0.35).

outcomes.statement: Suppressing SST+ interneurons lengthens CA1 SWRs, an effect not seen with PV+ suppression, and the genotypes differ.
outcomes.source: Figure 3E; Results, SWR signatures, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: SST+ interneuron suppression increased SWR length, an effect not seen following PV+ interneuron suppression (Figure 3E)
outcomes.notes: SST-Cre lengthening of 0.024 log units, p = 0.011, not significant after Holm; PV-Cre p = 0.072; genotype test p = 0.30. 5 SD variant SST-Cre p = 0.0056.

outcomes.statement: With SST+ suppression the percentage of SWRs longer than 100 ms rises from 38.5% under vehicle to 49.6% under CNO.
outcomes.source: Results, SWR signatures, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: found an increase when SST+ interneurons were suppressed (% of SWRs > 100 ms: vehicle 38.5% vs CNO 49.6%, paired t test, t(15) = 3.67, p = 0.002)
outcomes.notes: Under readings (a) and (c), 38.1% vehicle and 40.7% CNO (paired t p = 0.030); the CNO value is below 49.6 +/- 4.96 under every reading with the valid SWRs. With every detected event and session means (b, d) both values are in tolerance (41.8 and 45.0%) but p = 0.070. No reading has both values in tolerance and p < 0.05. 14 SST-Cre mice.

outcomes.statement: PV+, but not SST+, interneuron suppression increases the instantaneous frequency of CA1 SWRs.
outcomes.source: Figure 3F; Results, SWR signatures, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: PV+, but not SST+, interneuron suppression increased the instantaneous frequency of SWRs (Figure 3F)
outcomes.notes: PV-Cre +4.2 Hz, p = 4.5e-05 (logged p = 3.6e-05); SST-Cre p = 0.063 (0.061). Genotype test, reported only, p = 0.97. The 5 SD variant agrees.

outcomes.statement: PV+, but not SST+, suppression increases sharp-wave amplitude in CA1, and the genotypes differ.
outcomes.source: Figure 3G; Results, SWR signatures, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: PV+, but not SST+, interneuron suppression increased the instantaneous frequency of SWRs (Figure 3F) and sharp-wave (SW) amplitude in CA1 (Figure 3G)
outcomes.notes: PV-Cre increase p = 7.8e-08, but SST-Cre also increases significantly (p = 0.00207, below the first Holm threshold 0.00208) and the genotype test is not significant (p = 0.53; 0.15 with 5 degrees of freedom). Every CA1-sr site, the 5 SD variant, the trace without its mean removed and the deviation from a 200 ms pre-event baseline agree (SST-Cre p 0.00016 to 0.0021). The offset at the SW site is small (median raw LFP 39 file units against a median SW amplitude of 3274). Vehicle means are 3246 (PV-Cre) and 2999 (SST-Cre) file units against Table S4's 375 and 385 uV, about 8 times larger, which the Methods do not explain.
deviations: Reading (a) uses the CA1-sr site on the shank of the SWR site; the claims file leaves the site open.
The 0-30 Hz trace has its mean over rest removed before the Hilbert envelope; the trace as filtered and a pre-event baseline are variants, and give the same result.

outcomes.statement: SWR size is smaller when PV+ interneurons are suppressed, despite no change in CA1 MUA recruitment.
outcomes.source: Figure S2A; Results, SWR signatures, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: SWR size was smaller when PV+ interneurons were suppressed (Figure S2A) despite no change in CA1 MUA recruitment
outcomes.notes: PV-Cre -0.42 SD, p = 2.1e-05 (logged p = 0.00014); SST-Cre p = 0.50; 5 SD variant p = 2.5e-07. The statement's "no change in CA1 MUA recruitment" holds (fig3b, PV-Cre p = 0.12).

outcomes.statement: Suppressing PV+ interneurons modestly increases the incidence of rare fast ripples in CA1 (0.0004 to 0.0035 Hz), with no change in SST-Cre mice.
outcomes.source: Results, SWR signatures, paragraph 3; Table S2, Fast Ripple Rate
outcomes.quote: we did detect a modest increase in the incidence of rare fast ripples when PV+ interneurons were suppressed (Table S2)

statistics.test: Wilcoxon matched pairs signed rank test
Wilcoxon matched pairs signed rank test

outcomes.notes: The deposited LFP is band-passed at 0.1 to 300 Hz and sampled at 1 kHz; the paper's fast ripple detection needs 125 to 600 Hz at 5 kHz, and the wide-band data are not deposited.

outcomes.statement: The SWR rate changes are not due to differences in SWR detection (ripple band mean and SD) or in baseline MUA, which do not change with treatment in either genotype.
outcomes.source: Results, SWR signatures, paragraph 3; Table S2
outcomes.quote: This effect was not due to differences in SWR detection or baseline MUA (Table S2)

statistics.test: Wilcoxon matched pairs signed rank test

Wilcoxon matched pairs signed rank test
Wilcoxon matched pairs signed rank test
Wilcoxon matched pairs signed rank test
Wilcoxon matched pairs signed rank test

outcomes.notes: Nine of ten tests are not significant (ripple band mean and SD p from 0.22 to 0.74). Rest CA1 MUA in SST-Cre mice fails the normality or variance check, so the Table S2 rule takes the Wilcoxon test, p = 0.049 (paired t p = 0.18; 13.0 against 8.2 spikes/s). The failure is marginal.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing PV+ interneurons raises SG power in CA1 across all rest and raises its variance in CA1, CA3 and DG; suppressing SST+ interneurons does not change baseline SG power.
outcomes.source: Results, SWR-coincident SG, paragraph 2; Table S2, Rest SG Freq. Mean and SD
outcomes.quote: Following suppression of PV+ interneurons, SG power in CA1 was higher across all rest during CNO epochs (Figure 4A) – consistent with increased CA3 drive (Kemere et al., 2013) – and had higher variance in all 3 subregions (Table S3)

statistics.test: Wilcoxon matched pairs signed rank test

outcomes.notes: PV-Cre CA1-sr SG power rises (Wilcoxon p = 0.0005) and its SD rises in CA1-sr, CA3 and DG (p from 0.0002 to 0.02) under both readings. SST-Cre baseline SG power does not change in CA1-sr (p = 0.61) but falls in CA3 (p = 0.0023) and DG (p = 0.04), which the claim excludes. Measured values are the multitaper reading with file values scaled by 0.195 uV per unit, outside 109.51 +/- 10.95 and 127.6 +/- 12.76; unscaled values are 3422 and 5060. 13 PV-Cre mice have a CA1-sr site.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing PV+ interneurons increases SWR-coincident SG power in CA1, CA3 and DG, while suppressing SST+ interneurons does not change it; the genotypes differ in CA1.
outcomes.source: Figure 4D, Figure S2B; Results, SWR-coincident SG, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Suppressing PV+ interneurons led to greater SWR-coincident SG power in CA1, CA3, and DG ... as suppressing SST+ interneurons did not change SG power either at baseline (Table S2) or during SWRs
outcomes.notes: CNO sessions z-scored by the mouse's previous vehicle session. PV-Cre SWR-coincident SG power rises in CA1 (p = 1.3e-11, 13 of 13 mice) and CA3 (p = 0.00046), not significantly in DG (p = 0.19). No SST-Cre effect is significant (CA1 p = 0.0095, CA3 0.23, DG 0.14). The CA1 genotype test is not significant (p = 0.11; 0.013 with 5 degrees of freedom), so the partial rule fails. Empty vector mice also rise in CA1 (p = 1.6e-05), which may come from z-scoring a CNO session by another session's statistics or from session order; no output separates the two. With every session z-scored by its own statistics (code) no PV-Cre effect is significant (CA1 coefficient -0.06, p = 0.044).
deviations: Multitaper power over 30-50 Hz in the 100 ms after SWR onset with 3 tapers, time-bandwidth 2; the paper gives the 100 ms window but not the tapers. This is an assumption.

Z-scoring by the mean and SD of the same measure over the non-overlapping 100 ms windows of rest; a CNO session by the mouse's latest earlier vehicle session (Methods; in cohort 3 the vehicle sessions all come first, so this is the third vehicle session), a vehicle session by its own (claims file).
A region's value per SWR is the mean of its sites' z values (CA1-sr, CA3, DG).

outcomes.statement: Only PV+ suppression enhances the increase in SG coherence between CA1 and CA3 and between CA1 and DG during SWRs.
outcomes.source: Figure 4E; Results, SWR-coincident SG, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Similarly, only PV+ suppression enhanced the increase in SG coherence between CA1 and CA3 or DG during SWRs, (Figure 4E)
outcomes.notes: The SWR-related change in SG coherence does not rise with PV+ suppression (CA1-CA3 coefficient -0.0013, p = 0.82; CA1-DG +0.0006, p = 0.88). SST-Cre effects are not significant (p = 0.038 and 0.082) and neither genotype test is (p = 0.077 and 0.60). 207,869 of 295,070 SWRs have no other SWR in the 400 ms before onset.
deviations: Coherence between the CA1 SWR site and each CA3 or DG site, averaged over the region's pairs per SWR; the paper does not say which pairs.
Multitaper coherence with 3 tapers, time-bandwidth 2, over 30-50 Hz; an assumption, as for fig4d.

outcomes.statement: Across PV-Cre mice, the CNO-induced change in CA1 SWR-coincident SG power predicts the change in SW amplitude and the change in SWR frequency.
outcomes.source: Figure S2C-D; Results, SWR-coincident SG, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: the extent of CA1 SWR-coincident SG power increase correlated across animals with the extent of SW amplitude increase and the extent of SWR frequency increase (Figure S3C–D)

statistics.about: SG power change against SW amplitude change
SG power change against SWR frequency change

outcomes.notes: Across 13 PV-Cre mice the change in CA1 SWR-coincident SG power correlates positively but not significantly with the change in SW amplitude (r = 0.36, p = 0.23) and in SWR frequency (r = 0.42, p = 0.15) under both readings; R2 0.13 and 0.18 against 0.55 and 0.44. One PV-Cre mouse has no CA1-sr site. The SG power rests on the assumptions of fig4d-swr-sg-power-pv.
deviations: CA1 SWR-coincident SG power as in fig4d-swr-sg-power-pv (3 tapers, CNO sessions z-scored by the previous vehicle session), an assumption; SW amplitude and SWR frequency as in fig3g and fig3f.

outcomes.statement: Only a subset of CA3 SWRs, 37.18% averaged over vehicle sessions of PV-Cre and SST-Cre mice, overlap in time with CA1 SWRs.
outcomes.source: Results, local CA3 SWRs and DG spikes, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: only a subset of CA3 SWRs overlapped in time with CA1 SWRs (37.18%, averaged over all PV-Cre and SST-Cre vehicle sessions)
outcomes.notes: 25.3% averaged over 96 vehicle sessions (25.0% pooled over 75,767 CA3 SWRs), against 37.18 +/- 3.72; sessions range from 5.8 to 49.4%.
deviations: CA3 SWR site is the CA3 MUA site when it is in pyr, otherwise the first ca3-pyr site on its shank; the labels do not mark the CA3 pyramidal centre.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing either class increases CA3 MUA recruitment to CA3 SWRs and lengthens CA3 SWRs; PV+ suppression decreases CA3 SWR rate and CA3 SWR instantaneous frequency.
outcomes.source: Figure S3B-E; Results, local CA3 SWRs and DG spikes, paragraphs 1-2
outcomes.quote: Suppressing PV+ interneurons decreased CA3 SWR rate, while suppressing SST+ interneurons increased CA3 SWR rate (Figure S3C) ... Suppression of either interneuron type increased CA3 SWR length (Figure S3D). Finally, PV+ interneuron suppression decreased CA3 SWR instantaneous frequency (Figure S3E)

statistics.about: CA3 MUA to CA3 SWRs, PV-Cre
CA3 MUA to CA3 SWRs, SST-Cre

outcomes.notes: Reading (a), all CA3 SWRs, one of six tests holds (PV-Cre rate decrease, p = 0.00019); MUA (p = 0.76, 0.68), length (0.29, 0.15) and PV-Cre frequency (0.17) do not. Reading (b) none holds. The MUA part rests on the clock alignment.
deviations: CA3 MUA uses spike times shifted per session to the CA1 SWRs, as in fig3b-mua-during-swr; this is an assumption.
CA3 SWR site as in ca3-swr-overlap.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing SST+ interneurons increases CA3 SWR rate.
outcomes.source: Results, local CA3 SWRs and DG spikes, paragraph 2; Figure S3C
outcomes.quote: while suppressing SST+ interneurons increased CA3 SWR rate (Figure S3C)

statistics.about: CA3 SWR rate, PV vs SST

outcomes.notes: The SST-Cre effect is a non-significant decrease under both readings (-1.1/min, p = 0.051; -0.60/min, p = 0.039 for overlapping CA3 SWRs), consistent with the legend's p = 0.77, not with the text.

outcomes.statement: DG MUA during dentate spikes does not change; suppressing either class decreases dentate spike rate; PV+ suppression increases dentate spike length and decreases their amplitude, while SST+ suppression has no detectable effect on these.
outcomes.source: Figure S3F-I; Results, local CA3 SWRs and DG spikes, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Instead, DS MUA did not change (Figure S3F) ... Suppression of either PV+ or SST+ interneurons decreased DS rate (Figure S3G) ... Suppressing PV+ interneurons also increased DS length while decreasing DS amplitude, while suppressing SST+ interneurons had no detectable effect on these features
outcomes.notes: Five of eight parts hold (DS MUA unchanged p = 0.97 and 0.26; PV-Cre amplitude decrease p = 3.4e-05; SST-Cre length and amplitude unchanged after Holm). DS rate does not fall in either genotype (p = 0.40 and 0.071, SST-Cre coefficient positive) and PV-Cre length does not rise (p = 0.91). The detection as the Methods describe it finds 8.58 events per second of rest, close to Table S4's dentate spike rates of 9.18 (PV-Cre) and 8.45 Hz (SST-Cre), which supports this reading of the Methods. The amplitude is in z units, where Table S4 gives uV.
deviations: Dentate spikes from every peak of the z-scored 5 to 100 Hz trace during rest, amplitude to the nearest minimum, kept with z-scored log amplitude above 0.75 and length 5 to 25 ms (Methods, Analysis of neural data, paragraph 6); the z-scoring over rest and peak finding are assumptions.

outcomes.statement: During movement, suppressing either class increases MUA in DG and CA3 but not in CA1.
outcomes.source: Figure 5B; Results, SG during movement, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: suppressing either class increased MUA during movement in DG and CA3, but not CA1 (Figure 5B)
outcomes.notes: CA1 unchanged after correction (p = 0.14 and 0.046); CA3 and DG do not increase, all four coefficients negative (p from 0.09 to 0.82). 8 PV-Cre and 7 SST-Cre mice. Position and LFP agree to within about 2 s on the track (theta/delta power against speed peaks at zero lag, mean r 0.134 against 0.009 at 30 s or more); the sub-second spike offset could be checked in only 24 of 170 sessions (clear CA1 MUA peak around still-period SWRs), too few for the shifted variant to give a test.

outcomes.statement: During movement, suppressing PV+ interneurons amplifies SG power in CA1 with no effect in DG and CA3, while suppressing SST+ interneurons dampens SG power in DG and CA3 with no effect in CA1; all these effects differ between genotypes.
outcomes.source: Figure 5D, Figure S4A; Results, SG during movement, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Suppressing PV+ interneurons in DG and CA3 amplified SG power in CA1, but there was no detectable effect following suppression of SST+ interneurons. By contrast, suppressing PV+ interneurons had no detectable effect on SG power in DG and CA3, while suppressing SST+ interneurons dampened SG power locally in DG and CA3
outcomes.notes: Five of nine parts hold (SST-Cre decreases in CA3 p = 0.00064 and DG p = 1.2e-06; the three absences). The PV-Cre CA1 increase does not (coefficient -0.10, p = 0.71), nor any genotype test (p = 0.19, 0.45, 0.44).

outcomes.statement: During movement, suppressing PV+ interneurons enhances SG coherence between CA1 and CA3.
outcomes.source: Figure 5E; Results, SG during movement, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Relatedly, suppressing PV+ interneurons enhanced SG coherence between CA1 and CA3 (Figure 5E)
outcomes.notes: CA1-CA3 SG coherence decreases with PV+ suppression (per bin -0.034, p = 0.0024; over sessions -0.077, p = 0.00024).
deviations: Coherence between the CA1 SWR site and each CA3 site, averaged over pairs; the claims file names CA1-pyr and CA3 sites without saying which pairs.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing PV+, but not SST+, interneurons reduces SG frequency during movement in CA1, CA3 and DG, and the genotypes differ.
outcomes.source: Figure 5F, Figure S4B; Results, SG during movement, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: suppressing PV+ interneurons, but not SST+ interneurons, reduced SG frequency throughout the hippocampus (Figure 5F and S4B)
outcomes.notes: Peaks pooled over each region's sites: PV-Cre decreases in CA3 (p = 0.0087) and DG (p = 0.033) do not pass Holm, CA1 p = 0.44; SST-Cre no effect (p 0.30 to 0.75). One site per region: PV-Cre CA3 decrease p = 0.00099, CA1 p = 0.30, DG p = 0.13. The partial rule needs CA1 under both readings. All 8 PV-Cre and 7 SST-Cre mice are included. Genotype tests p 0.11 to 0.998 (0.013 to 0.93 with 5 degrees of freedom). Refitted to the likelihood maximum (fit check), the pooled PV-Cre decreases in CA3 (p = 0.00066) and DG (p = 0.0015) pass Holm and the DG genotype test passes with 5 degrees of freedom (p = 0.00019), but CA1 does not change (p = 0.14); same outcome.
deviations: Frequency from the interpeak intervals of every site of a region, pooled (Method M averages a region over its sites; Table S3's data-point counts imply peaks from several sites); one site per region (CA1 SWR site, the CA3 and DG MUA sites when they are among the region's sites, else the first site) is a variant. Version 1 of this attempt used one site and silently dropped mice whose DG or CA3 MUA site was not a region site; this is fixed.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing PV+ interneurons increases theta modulation of SG locally in DG and CA3 but not in CA1, while suppressing SST+ interneurons reduces theta modulation of SG in CA1, and these effects differ between genotypes.
outcomes.source: Figure 5G, Figure S4C; Results, SG during movement, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: suppressing PV+ interneurons increased theta modulation of SG only locally in DG and CA3, while suppressing SST+ interneurons reduced theta modulation of SG in CA1, and these effects were again detectably different between genotypes
outcomes.notes: PV-Cre theta modulation of SG decreases in CA3 (p = 0.018) and DG (p = 0.00098), the opposite of the claim; SST-Cre CA1 +0.02 (p = 0.56); genotype tests p = 0.51.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing SST+ interneurons amplifies FG power in CA1 and DG during movement, an effect specific to this class.
outcomes.source: Figure 6B, Figure S4D; Results, FG during movement, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Suppressing SST+ interneurons amplified FG power in CA1 and DG, an effect specific to this interneuron class (Figure 6A–B and S5D)
outcomes.notes: SST-Cre FG power falls in CA1 (p = 0.080) and significantly in DG (p = 1.1e-05); genotype tests p = 0.54 and 0.69.

outcomes.statement: In DG and CA3 of SST-Cre mice, the CNO-induced change in SG power predicts the change in FG power, animals with the greatest SG suppression showing the greatest FG enhancement.
outcomes.source: Figure S4E; Results, FG during movement, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: locally in DG and CA3, SG and FG showed an inverse relationship, where animals with the greatest SG suppression showed the greatest FG enhancement and vice versa (Figure S4E)
outcomes.notes: The SG and FG power changes of the 7 SST-Cre mice are positively correlated (CA3 r = 0.92, p = 0.0034; DG r = 0.81, p = 0.027, raw mean differences; the LMM conditional reading agrees), not negatively. Measured values are R2 under reading (a).

outcomes.statement: SST+ suppression decreases the SG/FG power ratio in CA1, PV+ suppression increases it throughout the hippocampus, and these effects differ between genotypes across the hippocampus.
outcomes.source: Figure 6E, Figure S4F; Results, FG during movement, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: these bidirectional changes in SG and FG power led to decreased SG/FG power ratios in CA1 following SST+ suppression and increased SG/FG power ratios throughout the hippocampus following PV+ suppression. These SG/FG ratio effects were significantly different between genotypes across the hippocampus
outcomes.notes: PV-Cre increases in CA3 (p = 0.00055) and DG (p = 0.00087) hold; PV-Cre CA1 (p = 0.32), SST-Cre CA1 (p = 0.14) and the three genotype tests (p = 0.17, 0.040, 0.051) do not.

outcomes.statement: FG coherence between CA1 and CA3 and between CA1 and DG does not change with either suppression.
outcomes.source: Figure 6F; Results, FG during movement, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: FG coherence, however, did not change (Figure 6F)
outcomes.notes: None of the four FG coherence effects is significant, per 1 s bin (p 0.20 to 0.50) or per session (p 0.23 to 0.90); coefficients -0.02 to +0.03.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing SST+ interneurons increases FG frequency throughout the hippocampus.
outcomes.source: Figure 6G, Figure S4G; Results, FG during movement, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: suppressing SST+ interneurons increased FG frequency throughout the hippocampus (Figure 6G and S4G)
outcomes.notes: Peaks pooled over each region's sites: SST-Cre FG frequency rises in CA3 (p = 1.4e-08) and DG (p = 2.2e-11), not significantly in CA1 (p = 0.013). One site per region, main fit: DG only in the deposited run (p = 2.2e-08; CA1 p = 0.81, CA3 0.24), no region in the run the verifier reviewed (DG p = 0.33); the fit stops short of the maximum at points that vary between runs. Refitted to the maximum, both readings give CA3 and DG (pooled p = 2.8e-07 and 2.4e-09, one site 3.5e-06 and 7.1e-09) and not CA1 (p = 0.0093 and 0.58). Pooled FG frequency rises in CA3 and DG in all 7 SST-Cre mice (t test of per-mouse changes p = 0.0031 and 0.0015).
deviations: Frequency from the interpeak intervals of every site of a region, pooled (Method M averages a region over its sites; Table S3's data-point counts imply peaks from several sites); one site per region (CA1 SWR site, the CA3 and DG MUA sites when they are among the region's sites, else the first site) is a variant. Version 1 of this attempt used one site and silently dropped mice whose DG or CA3 MUA site was not a region site; this is fixed.

Models fitted by L-BFGS-B from three starts, as in the rest of the attempt. For the per-peak frequency features this can stop short of the likelihood maximum at points that differ from run to run; the run notebook's fit check refits every run test with a Nelder-Mead search continuing from the best start and shows the outcome is the same.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing SST+ interneurons increases theta modulation of FG in CA1, an effect specific to SST+ interneurons.
outcomes.source: Figure 6H-J; Results, FG during movement, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: suppressing SST+ interneurons increased theta modulation of FG in CA1 (Figure 6H–J and S4H), an effect specific to SST+ interneurons
outcomes.notes: SST-Cre CA1 +0.073, p = 0.085; genotype test p = 0.15; PV-Cre -0.14, p = 0.067.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing PV+ interneurons dampens theta modulation of FG during movement.
outcomes.source: Results, theta during movement, paragraph 2; Figure S4H, Figure 6H; Discussion, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Overall, suppressing PV+ interneurons in DG and CA3 increased measures of CA3 coupling onto CA1, including enhancing SG power, coherence, and theta comodulation and dampening FG-theta comodulation
outcomes.notes: PV-Cre FG theta modulation falls in DG (p = 2.1e-06) and in CA3 with p = 0.0098, short of Holm; CA1 negative, p = 0.067.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing either PV+ or SST+ interneurons increases theta power in CA1 but not in CA3 or DG during movement.
outcomes.source: Figure S5B; Results, theta during movement, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Contrary to our hypothesis, suppressing either PV+ or SST+ interneurons increased theta power in CA1 but not elsewhere (Figure S5A–B)
outcomes.notes: CA1 theta power does not rise (PV-Cre p = 0.34, SST-Cre p = 0.80, both coefficients negative); SST-Cre DG theta power falls significantly (p = 0.0015).

outcomes.statement: Neither interneuron type modifies theta coherence or theta frequency, except for an increase in theta frequency in DG of PV-Cre mice.
outcomes.source: Figure S5C-D; Results, theta during movement, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Neither interneuron type modified theta coherence (Figure S5C) or theta frequency (Figure S5D) save for an increase in theta frequency in PV-Cre mice in DG
outcomes.notes: Peaks pooled over each region's sites: PV-Cre DG theta frequency rises (+0.040 log units, p = 0.00049) and none of the other nine tests is significant (coherence p 0.015 to 0.47, frequency p 0.0071 to 0.55). With one site per region PV-Cre CA3 theta frequency is significant (p = 0.0011), which the claim excludes, so the outcome rests on the pooled reading. The refit to the likelihood maximum gives the same pooled results. DG theta frequency rises in all 8 PV-Cre mice (t test of per-mouse changes p = 0.014); referred to the number of mice the F test gives p = 0.010, which would not pass Holm over 36. The per-peak p-value rests on the per-peak degrees of freedom of the paper's code.
deviations: Frequency from the interpeak intervals of every site of a region, pooled (Method M averages a region over its sites; Table S3's data-point counts imply peaks from several sites); one site per region (CA1 SWR site, the CA3 and DG MUA sites when they are among the region's sites, else the first site) is a variant. Version 1 of this attempt used one site and silently dropped mice whose DG or CA3 MUA site was not a region site; this is fixed.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing both PV+ and SST+ interneurons cannot be told apart from suppressing PV+ interneurons only, except for theta modulation of SG in DG and CA3, which double suppression decreases.
outcomes.source: Figures S6 and S7, Table S5; Results, suppressing both, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: we were unable to detect a difference between suppressing both interneuron types and suppressing PV+ interneurons only except in the case of comodulation of SG by theta in DG and CA3. In this instance, suppressing both interneuron types decreased theta modulation of SG, an effect not observed when suppressing either type alone

statistics.about: theta modulation of SG, CA3, PV vs P/S
theta modulation of SG, DG, PV vs P/S

outcomes.notes: Of 58 features (22 rest, 36 run) only DG theta power differs between P/S and PV-Cre (reading a), but the claimed exceptions, theta modulation of SG in CA3 and DG, do not differ (p = 0.60, 0.52). The two CSD features exist only for cohort 1, which has no P/S mice.

outcomes.statement: Suppressing both interneuron types has largely distinct effects from suppressing SST+ interneurons only; the exceptions are FG frequency and CA1 FG power, which follow the direction of SST+ suppression.
outcomes.source: Figures S6 and S7, Table S5; Results, suppressing both, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: In contrast, suppressing both interneuron types had largely distinct effects from suppressing SST+ interneurons only. The exceptions were FG frequency and CA1 FG power, in which case suppressing both interneuron types followed the direction of suppressing SST+ interneurons alone

statistics.about: SWR instantaneous frequency, SST vs P/S
CA1 SG power during SWRs, SST vs P/S
CA1 FG power, SST vs P/S

outcomes.notes: P/S does not change CA1 FG power (p = 0.81) and raises FG frequency in CA3 (p = 8.5e-07) and DG (p = 1.8e-08) but not CA1 (p = 0.72). None of the eight SST vs P/S tests the claim needs is significant (SW amplitude p = 0.68, CA1 SWR-coincident SG power 0.41, SWR frequency 0.40, run features 0.28 to 1.0).

outcomes.statement: In mice injected with an empty vector, CNO and vehicle epochs do not differ.
outcomes.source: Figures S6 and S7, Table S5; Results, consistency, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: we treated mice injected with an empty vector as a control and observed no differences between vehicle and CNO treated epochs (Figure S5 and S6 and Table S5)
outcomes.notes: Empty vector mice change with CNO in 4 rest features (SWR rate, chains, SWR size, CA1 SWR-coincident SG power; p 2.9e-07 to 0.0017) and 9 run features (CA3 theta power; DG theta, SG and FG power, FG frequency, theta frequency, SG and FG theta modulation, theta coherence; refitted to the likelihood maximum also CA3 FG frequency). Every empty vector mouse had its vehicle sessions before its CNO sessions. Within the vehicle sessions alone, DG theta frequency drifts from the first to the third session (p = 0.00021); the other eight run changes do not (p 0.115 to 0.93), so session order explains only part of them.

outcomes.statement: Running speed does not differ between vehicle and CNO sessions (4.8 against 5.1 cm/s).
outcomes.source: Results, consistency, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: differences in LFP during movement were not due to differences in running speed (vehicle 4.8 cm/s vs CNO 5.1 cm/s, paired t test, t(29) = 1.31, p = 0.2)
outcomes.notes: Run speed 4.70 against 5.24 cm/s, both in tolerance, but t(29) = 2.69, p = 0.012. Over the whole session 0.96 against 1.51 cm/s, p = 8.4e-06. Speed is higher in the third vehicle session than in the first in every group (empty vector 4.28, 4.71, 5.39 cm/s; P/S 5.14, 4.72, 5.75 cm/s), before any CNO session.

outcomes.statement: During vehicle treatment, PV-Cre mice differ from SST-Cre mice in DG and CA3 SG frequency (lower) and SG/FG ratios (higher).
outcomes.source: Results, consistency, paragraph 2; Table S4
outcomes.quote: We did note, however, that PV-Cre had different DG and CA3 SG frequencies and SG/FG ratios from SST-Cre mice during vehicle treatment (Table S4)

F test of the LMM for genotype effects

outcomes.notes: Peaks pooled over each region's sites: PV-Cre lower SG frequency in CA3 (39.66 against 40.95 Hz, p = 0.00056) and DG (40.16 against 41.48 Hz, p = 0.00034), higher SG/FG ratio in CA3 (6.08 against 3.89, p = 0.00054) and DG (5.09 against 3.27, p = 0.00026), each passing Holm over 36; all eight means within tolerance. With one site per region (untransformed) neither frequency difference is significant (CA3 p = 0.31, DG p = 0.44); logged, CA3 is (p = 0.00052) and DG is not (p = 0.0063). The outcome rests on the pooled reading. The refit leaves the four p-values as they are; referred to the number of mice they would be 0.0029 to 0.0044, and Welch t tests of the per-mouse means give 0.0051 to 0.0070, none below 0.05/36.
deviations: Frequency from the interpeak intervals of every site of a region, pooled (Method M averages a region over its sites; Table S3's data-point counts imply peaks from several sites); one site per region (CA1 SWR site, the CA3 and DG MUA sites when they are among the region's sites, else the first site) is a variant. Version 1 of this attempt used one site and silently dropped mice whose DG or CA3 MUA site was not a region site; this is fixed.

outcomes.statement: During vehicle treatment, females have slightly larger SWR sizes than males, with no other sex differences.
outcomes.source: Results, consistency, paragraph 1; Table S6
outcomes.quote: Females had slightly larger SWR sizes than males during vehicle treatment epochs (Table S6), but there were otherwise no sex differences

statistics.test: F test of the LMM for sex effects

outcomes.notes: SWR size does not differ by sex in vehicle sessions (female minus male -0.08 SD, p = 0.52). No rest or run feature passes Holm; smallest p 0.033 (CA3 SWR length) and 0.011 (DG theta power).

outcomes.statement: Interneuron suppression has effects of the same direction and magnitude in both sexes on most features; the exceptions are SW amplitude with SST+ suppression (down in females, up in males), FG power with SST+ suppression (larger rise in females), and DG and CA3 MUA during movement (larger rise in females with suppression of either or both classes).
outcomes.source: Results, consistency, paragraph 1; Table S7
outcomes.quote: The effect of suppressing interneurons was in the same direction and magnitude in both sexes on most features (Table S7) with a few exceptions. Suppressing SST+ interneurons decreased SW amplitude in females but had the opposite effect in males, leading to no effect overall, and enhanced FG power to a greater degree in females than in males. Interestingly, suppressing either or both interneuron classes led to a greater increase in DG and CA3 MUA during movement in females
outcomes.notes: No named exception has a significant sex interaction (SST-Cre SW amplitude p = 0.40 with 3 female and 11 male mice; FG power and run MUA p 0.021 to 0.85). Significant interactions after Holm: PV-Cre CA3 SWR length at rest; PV-Cre CA1 FG frequency and SST-Cre CA1-CA3 theta coherence during run. The P/S track group has 6 female and 1 male mouse, so its interaction is not tested. Table S7 was not available, so the paper's own list cannot be compared.

findings.statement: The MUA spike times are not on the clock of the LFP. CA1 MUA peaks around the SWRs detected on the LFP in 261 of 311 analysed home cage sessions, but displaced from the SWR midpoint by a session-specific lag (median -0.145 s, quartiles -0.395 to -0.055 s, range about -2 to +1 s, the MUA earlier in most sessions); only 26 sessions have the peak within 20 ms. With the deposited times the mean normalised CA1 MUA during SWRs is 0.39 SD (median -0.2); with each session shifted by its lag, 1.73 SD.

Four 4-shank mice (Beverly and Worf, PV-Cre; Picard and Riker, SST-Cre) have only home cage sessions labelled CNO, numbered 8 to 17, so they have no vehicle sessions as deposited; the paper analyses 16 PV-Cre and 16 SST-Cre mice with vehicle and CNO.

In cohort 3 every mouse has its vehicle sessions before its CNO sessions, on the track and in the home cage, where the Methods say the treatments alternated; cohort 2 alternates. Either the labels or the description is wrong. As deposited, treatment is confounded with session order, and the empty vector mice change with CNO in 4 rest and 9 run features, and run faster on CNO days.

The scale of the LFP values is unclear. The unit attribute says microvolts, and the ripple-band envelope over rest (mean 68.8 file units over 311 home cage sessions) is close to Table S2's 72.39 uV. But the SW amplitude in vehicle sessions is about 3000 file units against Table S4's 375 and 385 uV, the rest SG power matches Table S2 neither in file units nor scaled by 0.195, and values reach the int16 limits in 123 of 311 home cage sessions.
The session start times of the linear track files put all sessions of a mouse within minutes of each other (shortest gap 0.9 to 4.6 min in all 30 mice), which cannot be right for 25 min sessions.
Session Chakotay01 (home cage) is deposited twice, as sub-Chakotay_ses-Chakotay01-HomeCage and sub-Chakotay_ses-Chakotay01_HomeCage, with the same LFP length, spike count and start time.
Home cage sessions of cohort 3 last about 25 min and track sessions about 25 min, where the Methods give 60 and 30 min; many cohort 2 mice have 7 home cage sessions where the Methods give 6.
Every unit's spike train begins with a spike at exactly 0.0 s (about 31 per session, one per site), which is not a recorded spike.

The electrode location labels carry undocumented tokens ("ca1-pyr 1", "mua", "dg-val gc"). They were read as the SWR detection site, the highest-MUA site of a region, and DG sites with confirmed dentate spikes, from the Methods' wording; the dandiset does not say so. The session description says "1 hour after CNO injection" for vehicle sessions too.

On the linear track, position and LFP agree to within about 2 s: the log theta/delta power ratio correlates with speed at zero lag (mean r 0.134, positive in 141 of 170 sessions) and not with speed shifted by 30 s or more (mean 0.009). The sub-second spike offset found in the home cage could be checked on the track in only 24 of 170 sessions, those with a clear CA1 MUA peak around SWRs in still periods (median lag -0.245 s).

paper_notes.statement: Question for the authors. The dentate spike detection as the Methods describe it (peaks of the z-scored 5-100 Hz trace, amplitude to the nearest minimum, z-scored log amplitude above 0.75, length 5 to 25 ms) finds 8.58 events per second of rest, close to Table S4's rates of 9.18 and 8.45 Hz. Table S4 gives the dentate spike amplitude in uV, where the Methods z-score the trace. On which trace and in which units was the amplitude measured?

Question for the authors. The Methods log-transform features "when errors were not Gaussian" and the figure code logs every feature. Which features were logged for the published LMMs, and how were SWR start and end defined (the Methods give only the 3 SD, 15 ms rule)?
Question for the authors. The deposited spike times are offset from the LFP (see the format_error finding). Which clock alignment did the analysis use, and can the aligned times be deposited?

Question for the authors. Which tapers did the SWR-triggered spectrogram and coherence use (the Methods give the 100 ms window), and were vehicle epochs z-scored by their own statistics? Was instantaneous frequency during run pooled over the sites of a region, or taken at one site?

entries.name: jones-2021
entries.title: Hippocampal LFP after suppressing DG and CA3 interneurons (Aery Jones et al. 2021)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Aery Jones et al. (2021) on dandiset 000165, which holds the LFP, MUA spike times and position of PV-Cre, SST-Cre, PV-Cre/SST-Cre and empty vector mice in home cage and linear track sessions after vehicle or CNO. It tests the SWR, CA3 SWR and dentate spike features at rest, the gamma, theta and MUA features during running, the double suppression, empty vector and sex comparisons, and the CSD during SWRs of cohort 1, with the paper's linear mixed models.
